sn40.2:0.3: A Question About the Second Absorption
sn40.2:1.1: “They speak of this thing called the ‘second stage of meditation’.
sn40.2:1.2: What is the second stage of meditation?
sn40.2:1.4: ‘As thinking and considering are stilled, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the second stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of concentration, with internal clarity and poise, without thinking and considering.
sn40.2:1.5: This is called the second stage of meditation.’
sn40.2:1.6: And so … I was entering and remaining in the second stage of meditation.
sn40.2:1.7: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by thinking beset me.
sn40.2:2.1: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,
sn40.2:2.3: Don’t neglect the second stage of meditation, brahmin! Settle your mind in the second stage of meditation; unify your mind and concentrate it in the second stage of meditation.’
sn40.2:2.4: And so, after some time … I entered and dwelled in the second stage of meditation.
sn40.2:2.5: So if anyone should be rightly called
sn40.2:2.6: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
